body: - 2026-11-08: A Python edit script that writes a backslash-escaped quote (`\"`) into Rust source carries it in a raw string `r'…'`, or the edit goes through the Edit tool — a plain Python string turns `\"` into `"` with no error, so a Rust `r#"…"#` expectation changes silently and its test reads red.

body:
Chunk 2026-11-07-ui-graph built one read of a screen's UI graph: per snapshot node its stable id, owner, component, current handlers and their declared and confirmed state writes, and per registered state its writers and reading components.
It added the snapshot field NodeState.clickable (after focused): true where the walk's current listeners hold click and the element is no disabled form control, with the text token clickable written only when true and Reading::Clickable (Reading::ALL twelve).
The click reading that a11y-plan states as not built and owed to the route entry The UI graph is now built, and residual res-gvelrxja's disposition is met.
It added the graph verb on every carrier (socket, command line, MCP, kept check): VERBS 12 to 13, instance verbs 8 to 9, NODE_FIELDS 13 to 14, FieldKind 10 to 12, and it reserved a fifth stable-id form {owner}///{key} (virtual_node_id) that no caller produces.
It measured: run stand 244 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; stand files 51 to 52 (new stand_graph); dioxus-native-dom unit tests 83 to 100; the Cells screen 53,859 B in 740 lines and 6 parts (was 5); the Cells graph answer 293,869 B.
Roles, names, Tab orders and unkeyed_actionable read as before; no served screen's markup moved; no master was edited by the chunk.

The actionable-key rule's clause that no snapshot field says an element reacts to a click, its field owed to the route entry The UI graph: now stale, the field is built as NodeState.clickable and residual res-gvelrxja's disposition is met (body row and screen-reader-support rows 46 and 47).
The click-field row in ci-integration (row 21) that describes the reacts-to-a-click reading as owned by the route entry and not built: stale.
Every a11y-plan count of the snapshot's node keys: 13 to 14 (three rows), clickable joining after focused.

The snapshot model statement (what the snapshot takes from the tree and from the element, and that its text form, parts, diff, MCP results and node-key help read that model alone): clickable now comes from the vdom walk's current listeners and the element's disabled state, still the one snapshot model with no second role mapping.

The listener mark's over-inclusion note (an element whose listener was removed still marked, conservative): clickable reads current listeners, so a removed listener no longer reads clickable; the mark itself is unchanged and its count stays 677.

The stable element id / author_id grammar: a fifth, reserved form {owner}///{key} (VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR, virtual_node_id) is stated, no tier can hold ///, and no served id holds it; every existing id reads as before.
The unkeyed_actionable check and the stand's roles, names and Tab orders: re-read and unmoved (returns nothing on every stand task).
The verb and carrier counts where a11y-plan cites them (the lint verb on every carrier): VERBS 12 to 13, instance verbs 8 to 9, graph listed after lint; lint is still the eighth instance verb.

The stand test inventory and tallies: a new stand file stand_graph (stand files 51 to 52), run stand 244 passed 0 failed 7 ignored, and a CLICKABLE table in stand_non_lean_tasks, in both layout modes.
The stand-repeat leg's file set: its stand_* glob now takes stand_graph; stand_graph is not added to the a11y leg's file list.
The Cells screen figures where a11y-plan cites them: 47,089 to 53,859 bytes, 740 lines, 5 to 6 parts.
The dioxus-native-dom unit test count where cited: 83 to 100; the 83 percent coverage floor is a different claim and unchanged.

The Dioxus bridge's event path (framework exposure of Enter, Space and click dispatch): DioxusEventHandler::handle_event now sets and clears a SignalRegistry dispatch around runtime.handle_event where a registry exists; with no registered state it dispatches as before.
The disabled-form-control rule now has one more reader: clickable is false on an ElementData::is_disabled form control; the rule itself is unchanged.
The capability statement's not-built line for a snapshot field saying an element reacts to a click was removed; any a11y-plan text citing that line as an open gap is stale.

body_fields.fact: NodeState.clickable is a bool after focused, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold click and the element is no disabled form control, written in the text form as the token clickable only when true, always written in JSON beside focused, and a diff reading Reading::Clickable (Reading::ALL twelve).
On the stand clickable reads true on counter-increment and on each of Cells' 676 cells, and false on counter-value and cells-grid, from the one snapshot model and not from the listener mark.

stand_non_lean_tasks asserts a CLICKABLE table of clickable elements without a role per task in both layout modes: Counter, Temperature Converter, Flight Booker, Timer and CRUD 0 each, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676.

DioxusDocument::graph (behind accessibility) is a read-only UiGraph with one GraphNode per snapshot node in pre-order (id, owner, component, handlers, reads) and per registered state its declared writes, confirmed or flagged writers and reading components; an option's or optgroup's owner is the stable id of its select; the answer carries ids, component names, state names, event names, closed flag words and booleans only.
stand_graph asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node, that no served id holds the reserved separator ///, and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text.

Apps register state for the graph through use_graph_state (dioxus-native-dom) with authored DeclaredWrite declarations, wrapped in seven_guis as use_graph_signal; a write is resolved to the first element of its dispatch chain carrying a listener of its event and flagged undeclared or unconfirmed, unconfirmed only once the handler's event has been dispatched through its element.

body_fields.fact: DioxusDocument::graph(&self) -> UiGraph (behind accessibility) is read-only. UiGraph {nodes, states} has one GraphNode {id, owner, component, handlers, reads} per snapshot node in pre-order, GraphHandler {event, writes}, GraphWrite {state, declared, confirmed, flag}, GraphState {name, component, declared, writers, readers}, GraphWriter {id, event, declared, confirmed, flag}, and WriteFlag::{Undeclared, Unconfirmed} with word().

Graph semantics: owner is the stable id of BaseDocument::select_of for an option or optgroup. A repeated (name, component) registration reads {name}:{k}. readers names each reading component once, in the pre-order of its first node, and a state only the app root reads appears in its nodes' reads alone. writers lists only writes a run confirmed or flagged, while declared keeps the authored declaration. A write resolves to the first chain element carrying a listener of its event, or to nothing when an earlier chain node is gone. unconfirmed fires only after a dispatch of the handler's event passed through its element and no run wrote the state.

use_graph_state(name: &'static str, writers: &'static [DeclaredWrite], subscribers: Subscribers) takes dioxus-core types alone. The first registering hook provides a SignalRegistry context at ScopeId::ROOT. Each entry holds a ReactiveContext::new_with_callback that records one write against the standing dispatch (chain head first, its event name) and the writing scope, and leaves with its scope via use_drop. DeclaredWrite {id, event} names a stable id or a prefix ending in *, and an event without on. The registry's Debug prints counts alone.

The Signal-returning use_graph_signal(name, writers, init) lives in seven_guis tasks/mod.rs, not in dioxus-native-dom, because dioxus-native-dom names no crate defining Signal and the manifest freeze forbids adding one. tasks::writes(id, event) is a const fn.

The graph verb's JSON answer is written by hand in the json module as {"nodes":[{id,owner?,component?,handlers:[{event,writes:[{state,declared,confirmed,flag?}]}],reads}],"states":[{name,component?,declared:[{id,event}],writers:[{id,event,declared,confirmed,flag?}],readers}]}. An argument is refused malformed with nothing run, and the answer feeds the record of ids from the graph's node ids.

The graph is unpaged: graph takes no argument and answers the whole screen at once. Cells reads 293,869 bytes (547,685 at first build and 522,692 after the readers narrowing), under the answer bound held by stand_graph. The remainder, each cell's declared click writes, is the stated limit An unpaged graph, owned by residual res-7cc5bi4k.

stand_graph runs in both layout modes. It holds the verb equal to DioxusDocument::graph, every graph node to a snapshot node, no served id to the /// form, a graph read to change nothing and hold no typed text, and the Cells answer to the bound. GRAPH_DRIVES in tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs drives each conditional write once, so no stand write reads a flag.

CLICKABLE counts per served task, in both layout modes (stand_non_lean_tasks): Counter, Flight Booker, Timer, CRUD and Temperature Converter 0 each, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676. The listener mark's count stays 677.

In Dioxus 0.7.10 an async event handler's spawned task runs inside the dispatch that started it, so its signal writes are recorded against that event. dioxus-signals keeps a reactive context subscribed while mark_dirty returns true, so the registry's watcher needs no re-subscribe.
A &'static [DeclaredWrite] slice built from const fn calls is written const { &[...] }. A bare &[writes(..)] is a temporary that is not promoted to 'static and errors E0716.

body:
The session added a read-only UI graph of a screen: a new driver verb graph that answers each snapshot node's id, owner, component, handlers with their declared and confirmed writes, and each registered state's writers and readers.
It added a snapshot field clickable (NodeState.clickable, text token clickable after focused), true where an element has a click listener and is no disabled form control; the capability line that said this reading was not built was retired.
Counts moved: VERBS 12 to 13 (instance verbs 8 to 9, graph after lint), NODE_FIELDS 13 to 14, FieldKind 10 to 12, Reading::ALL 11 to 12, describe's row to 13, 14, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15, the MCP listing to 13 tools.
It added a state registry hook use_graph_state with DeclaredWrite declarations in dioxus-native-dom, a reserved virtual id form owner///key with virtual_node_id, and registered every seven_guis task's signals through use_graph_signal.
Measured: the Cells screen text went from 47,089 to 53,859 bytes in 6 parts (740 lines); the Cells graph answer reads 293,869 bytes, kept as the stated limit An unpaged graph; run stand reads 244 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
No dependency, manifest, blitz-dom, colour, font, layout or styling changed; no served screen's markup moved.

The cli surface's component patterns for escher-session and its mcp role: a new verb graph answers one uncoloured JSON line with exit status 0 on the command line and one JSON-RPC line over MCP; any text listing the driver's verbs or MCP tools now needs graph after lint.
Any count of the driver's verbs (12 to 13), instance verbs (8 to 9) or MCP tools (12 to 13) stated on the cli surface is stale.
The usage line and help on the cli surface gain graph after lint; a statement quoting the usage line or the tools/list order is stale.
Any count of a snapshot node's keys (13 to 14) is stale: clickable joins after focused, always written in a node's JSON and written as the text token clickable only when true.

The cli output contract (stdout holds only JSON, no colour or ESC byte, exit class 0, 1, 2, 3) now also covers the graph answer; a graph call with an argument is refused malformed with nothing run (exit class of a refusal).

A statement that no snapshot field says an element reacts to a click, or that the click reading is not built, is stale: NodeState.clickable now reads it from the element's own click listener, excluding a disabled form control.
Any figure for the Cells screen's snapshot text (47,089 bytes, 5 parts) is stale: it now reads 53,859 bytes, 740 lines, 6 parts.

Stable element id forms: a fifth reserved form owner///key (VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR, virtual_node_id) is stated, produced by no caller; any rule enumerating the id forms an agent reads on the cli surface now has it.

The Dioxus event path on every Dioxus document (desktop-native, mobile-native and web-spa launches through dioxus-native) now sets a registry dispatch around handle_event only where a state is registered; inert and unchanged where none is.

The seven_guis stand tasks' signals are now registered with declarations through use_graph_signal; any example-fixture text describing how those tasks hold their state with use_signal alone is stale (use_signal stays only in the stand shell and stand.rs linked).

body_fields.change: Add a Dioxus-integration row. The bridge's `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` sets the `SignalRegistry` dispatch (chain head first, and its event name) around `runtime.handle_event` and clears it after, but only when `runtime.has_context::<SignalRegistry>(ScopeId::ROOT)` holds. This changes the event path of every Dioxus document but does nothing without a registry: a page that registers no state reaches no registry and dispatches as before. The buffered render, `initial_build`, `poll` and `flush_queued_mounted_events` are untouched, and dioxus-core, the manifests and `mutation_writer.rs` are unchanged.
body_fields.sidecar: Dioxus integration: the bridge's dispatch now records against a registered state's registry, and does nothing without one (2026-11-07-ui-graph)
body_fields.rationale: The report's Symbols / APIs (the bridge dispatch) call this "a change on every Dioxus document's event path, inert without a registry". The arch outcome (fct-dvu6no2e) confirms that every manifest is unchanged and that mutation_writer.rs is byte-equal.

body_fields.change: Narrow the row's last clause. Hook-local `use_signal` state that is not registered stays unreachable without a fork-level change, because dioxus-core's `Scope.hooks` is `pub(crate)`. A state registered through `use_graph_state(name, writers, subscribers)` is reachable with no fork-level change and only dioxus-core's public types. Its readers are read from its `Subscribers`. Its writes are recorded by a `ReactiveContext::new_with_callback` subscribed to the signal, against the standing dispatch and the writing scope. `DioxusDocument::graph` reads both.
body_fields.sidecar: Held-signal readers: registered hook-local state is now reachable through public API, and unregistered state still is not (2026-11-07-ui-graph)
body_fields.rationale: The report's Symbols / APIs (the registry and the graph reader) show `use_graph_state` taking only dioxus-core types, and the Dependencies record no crate or manifest change. This contradicts the row's claim that hook-local state is "not reachable without a fork-level change" for any state the app registers.

body_fields.change:
- Graph semantics:
- `owner` is the stable id of `BaseDocument::select_of` for an option or optgroup.
- A repeated (name, component) registration reads `{name}:{k}`.
- `readers` names each reading component once, in the pre-order of its first node. A state only the app root reads appears in its nodes' `reads` alone.
- `writers` lists only writes a run confirmed or flagged, while `declared` keeps the authored declaration.
- A write resolves to the first chain element carrying a listener of its event, or to nothing when an earlier chain node is gone.
- `unconfirmed` fires only after a dispatch of the handler's event passed through its element and no run wrote the state.
body_fields.sidecar: standard-contracts bridge: graph semantics for owner, ordinal, readers, writers, resolution and unconfirmed (2026-11-07-ui-graph)
body_fields.rationale: These are the report's graph reader semantics, including the operator's fixes inputs#I7 and inputs#I8 and the stop at a gone node.

body_fields.change:
- The registry: `use_graph_state(name: &'static str, writers: &'static [DeclaredWrite], subscribers: Subscribers)` takes dioxus-core types alone.
- The first registering hook provides a `SignalRegistry` context at `ScopeId::ROOT`.
- Each entry holds a `ReactiveContext::new_with_callback`. The callback records one write against the standing dispatch (chain head first, and its event name) and the writing scope.
- An entry leaves with its scope through `use_drop`.
- `DeclaredWrite { id, event }` names a stable id or a prefix ending in `*`, and an event without `on`.
- The registry's `Debug` prints counts alone.

body:
The chunk 2026-11-07-ui-graph adds a thirteenth driver verb, graph, the ninth instance verb: one read of a screen's UI graph, giving each node's id, owner, component, handlers with declared and confirmed writes, and the states it reads. It answers over the socket, the command line, MCP and kept checks.
dioxus-native-dom gains two modules: graph (the read-only DioxusDocument::graph reader, UiGraph and its types, behind accessibility) and signal_registry (use_graph_state, SignalRegistry, DeclaredWrite). The bridge's event dispatch sets the registry's dispatch only where a registry is present.
The snapshot gains NodeState.clickable, a closed bool written after focused, so NODE_FIELDS goes 13 to 14, Reading::ALL 11 to 12 and FieldKind 10 to 12. The reserved id form {owner}///{key} and virtual_node_id are public.
seven_guis tasks register their signals through use_graph_signal with authored declarations, in all seven tasks. The stand gains stand_graph, so stand files go 51 to 52 and run stand goes from 244 · 0 · 7. The two committed counter checks were re-recorded.
Measured: the Cells graph answer is 293,869 bytes after two operator narrowings. The remainder is the stated limit An unpaged graph, residual res-7cc5bi4k. host_log and mcp_log read 0 needles with one graph call each, escher-driver still holds 2 info_span! sites, and CI is green on 2ce2820b.
Retired: the capability statement's Not built line for a snapshot field saying an element reacts to a click. No dependency, manifest, blitz-dom source or escher-telemetry file changed.

The command span: graph is a new word of its verb field. A graph call through Session::run opens the one command span and records verb alone: it runs no step, so no settled, passes or diff counts. The span's eight fields and the 2 info_span! sites are unchanged.

The tool_call span: its tool field gains graph, and the verb table is now thirteen words. graph is an instance verb, so its tool_call parents one command child. Rows naming twelve tools or eight instance verbs are stale.

The session library's verb list in the logging-stack and log-coverage prose names scroll sixth, screenshot seventh and lint eighth. graph is now the ninth instance verb, and rows counting eight instance verbs are stale. Rows naming lint the eighth still hold.

Outcome classes written by to_json alone and never logged or fielded: Outcome::Graphed joins Shot, Linted and Part. Its answer is the graph's JSON line on the command line and over MCP, and is kept whole in a recorded check. Outcome's Debug now covers the graph too.

The snapshot's state readings, which log-coverage and pii text describe as three closed words and booleans per node: NodeState.clickable is a further closed bool. It is written after focused, carried in the diff, and adds the text token clickable. Any node-key count of thirteen is now fourteen.

body:
The chunk 2026-11-07-ui-graph added a thirteenth driver verb, graph, an instance verb with no argument that answers the screen's UI graph: each snapshot node's id, owner, component, handlers with declared and confirmed writes, and the states it reads.
The graph answer carries ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, closed flag words (undeclared, unconfirmed) and booleans only, never a value. It crosses the socket, the command line, MCP and kept checks. This is a boundary widening, ratified by the founder's P4 fork 1 (inputs#I4) and halted on one Validate card before apply.
dioxus-native-dom gained a graph module (behind accessibility) and a signal_registry module (use_graph_state, SignalRegistry, DeclaredWrite). The bridge's event dispatch now sets the registry's dispatch on every Dioxus document, but only where a registry exists, so it is inert without one.
The snapshot gained NodeState.clickable, a closed bool written after focused, so NODE_FIELDS went from 13 to 14. VERBS went from 12 to 13 and instance verbs from 8 to 9. The stable-id grammar gained a reserved fifth form {owner}///{key}, spelled by the public virtual_node_id, which no walk calls.
Measured: the Cells graph answer is 293,869 bytes, within the answer bound. The unpaged size stays a stated limit, with residual res-7cc5bi4k (target next). No dependency, manifest, Cargo.lock, deny.toml or blitz-dom change was made, and mutation_writer.rs is byte-identical.
Retired: the capability statement's Not built line for a snapshot field saying an element reacts to a click.

The driver command schema's closed table of twelve verbs is now thirteen. graph is checked by validate as a verb with no argument, and an argument is refused malformed with nothing run. Any count of the verbs, the MCP tools or the driver commands as tools moves from twelve to thirteen.
The instance verbs went from eight to nine: graph is the ninth, after lint. Any row reading the eight instance verbs is stale. A row naming lint the eighth instance verb still holds.

The node keys went from thirteen to fourteen: clickable, a closed bool, joins after focused in the snapshot, its text token, diffs and the written node. It falls under the widening rule as a closed-value field inside an already ratified carrier.

The carriers of the driver session socket, the MCP stdio server and kept checks (ids, names, control values, snapshot text, diffs, screenshots, a lint's findings) now also carry a UI graph. That graph holds ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, closed flag words and booleans. This reaches the threat-model vectors for local IPC and local stdio, and the input-validation and API-security rows that list what a reply carries.

The stable element id contract gained a reserved fifth form {owner}///{key}. The public virtual_node_id returns None for an empty or slash-bearing key and is called by no walk. The id grammar states why no tier can hold the triple slash, and no served id holds it.

The two committed checks of the scripted stand-Counter sessions were re-recorded (the CLI check +4/-4 lines, the MCP check +6/-6) and still replay through the strict reader. A kept check may now hold a graph step and its answer.

The Dioxus bridge's event dispatch, on every Dioxus document, now sets and clears the registry's dispatch around runtime.handle_event, but only when a SignalRegistry context exists at the root scope. This is an engine-path change, inert without a registry. The buffered render, initial_build, poll and the mounted-event flush are untouched.
The MCP server answers the graph tool's call with the text block of its JSON line. graph is listed after lint because VERBS orders it. The listing and result code did not change.

escher-session's command-line usage line gains graph after lint. The command line answers graph with one uncoloured JSON line, status 0, so the stdout rule of one JSON line per command now covers graph.

Logging: graph's command span records verb alone, and its tool_call parents one command span. The driver still has 2 info_span sites. host_log and mcp_log read 0 id, name and graph needles at trace in both builds. The new files hold no log site, print or env read.

The cold-agent pipe's VERBS gains graph (thirteen), and its fake server answers graph with an empty nodes and states object. The verdict's capability-unused set is unchanged: graph is not required of a cold agent. A cold-agent check's steps are validated against the thirteen-verb schema.

Password and file-input masking: a sentinel typed into crud-name occurs 0 times in the graph answer, and the graph holds names only, never a control value. The masked-value rule is unmoved, and the graph is a carrier it must now cover.

Reply bounds: the graph answer is unpaged. Cells reads 293,869 bytes, within the answer bound, after it read 547,685 at first build and 522,692 after the readers narrowing. The plan's forecast of under 200 KB was disproved. The stated limit An unpaged graph and residual res-7cc5bi4k own the remaining size.

Line citations into dioxus-native-dom's snapshot and diff code moved: snapshot.rs gained lines at 77-80, 112-116, 134-135 and 199, ahead of a 278-305 citation, and snapshot_diff.rs gained lines at 55-56, 63 and 74, ahead of a :111 citation. The file-input masking row's citations shift.

Environment-read citations moved. tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs gained lines at 19 and 134-147, ahead of the :349 citation. examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs gained lines 4-5, ahead of the :28 citation. packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs gained lines at 399, 408 and 413-416, ahead of the 654-655 citation. The claims themselves are unmoved: the new code reads no env var.

Re-read unmoved: packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs is byte-identical to upstream 434e0661, so its try_element_to_node_id and element_to_node_id citations (41-49) and the panic-path claims on it stand.

The new in-process app API (use_graph_state, SignalRegistry, DeclaredWrite) is exported through dioxus-native's re-export of dioxus-native-dom. It takes dioxus-core types alone. Its Debug prints counts only, it holds no NodeId beyond the dispatch chain, and it has no unwrap on app input. This reaches any no-NodeId-kept, no-panic-on-input or no-log-site rule over dioxus-native-dom.

The graph reader DioxusDocument::graph is read-only: a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text (stand_graph, both layout modes). This reaches rules that a read verb runs no step and records ids only from what it answers.

The UI graph crossing the session socket, the command line, MCP and kept checks is a boundary widening, ratified by the founder's P4 fork 1 (Новый глагол graph, inputs#I4) and halted on one Validate card with one confirm before apply.

Markup attributes — the stable element id reserves a fifth form {owner}///{key} for virtual nodes; virtual_node_id spells it and returns None for an empty or slash-bearing key, no walk calls it, and no served id holds the triple slash.

Dioxus bridge dispatch — on every Dioxus document the event handler sets the SignalRegistry's dispatch around runtime.handle_event and clears it after, only where a registry context exists at the root scope; a page with no registered state reaches no registry and dispatches as before, an engine change inert without a registry.

Signal registry (dioxus-native-dom use_graph_state) — an in-process app API taking dioxus-core types alone; each entry leaves with its scope, its Debug prints counts only, it holds no NodeId beyond the dispatch chain, and it has no log site, print, env read or unwrap on app input.

Snapshot reading clickable — a closed bool, true where an element's current listeners hold click and it is no disabled form control, written after focused and in the text only when true; a closed-value field inside a ratified carrier, so no widening.
The graph answer is unpaged and takes no part argument; Cells reads 293,869 bytes within the answer bound, its size the stated limit An unpaged graph, owned by residual res-7cc5bi4k (target next).
The graph verb's command span records verb alone and its MCP tool_call parents one such span; host_log and mcp_log read 0 id, name and graph needles at trace with one graph call each, in both builds.
Cold-agent pipe — its VERBS holds graph (thirteen) and its fake server answers graph with empty nodes and states; graph is not required of a cold agent, and the capability-unused set is unchanged.

The snapshot gained NodeState.clickable after focused (NODE_FIELDS 13 to 14, Reading::ALL 11 to 12, FieldKind 10 to 12, describe row [13, 14, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15]); the capability statement's not-built click line was retired.

Measured: run stand 244 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 52 stand files; Cells screen 53,859 bytes, 740 lines, 6 parts; Cells graph answer 293,869 bytes, an unpaged-graph stated limit owned by residual res-7cc5bi4k; CI on HEAD green 17 of 17.
The dioxus-native-dom unit-test count moved from 83 to 100 #[test] functions: every row stating 83 unit tests is stale; the 83 % coverage floor rows share the token and stay true.

The dioxus-native-dom unit coverage list (snapshot builder, text form, parts, diff, stable id, bridge, mutation writer, events) now also covers the UI graph reader, the signal registry, the reserved virtual id form and the clickable reading.

The driver verb count moved from twelve to thirteen and the instance-verb count from eight to nine: graph sits after lint at the instance level; rows reading the twelve verbs or the eight instance verbs as today's count are stale, while a row naming lint the eighth instance verb stays true.
The node-key count moved from thirteen to fourteen: clickable joins after focused in NODE_FIELDS, the JSON node, the text token and the help of snapshot text and changed.
The describe count row moved from [12, 13, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15] to [13, 14, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15], stated in the scope summary and in the unit strategy.

The newest run stand reading moved from 237 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 51 files to 244 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 52 files, stand_graph picked up by its stand_ prefix with no script change; the CI-integration current stand-file count is stale too, while dated readings at earlier chunks stay historical.
The Cells screen text moved from 47,089 to 53,859 bytes and from 5 to 6 parts, its lines unmoved at 740; the stand Cells served check's PARTS constant reads 6.

The cold-agent pipe's verb set gained graph (thirteen): the allowed tool set the judge's valid_step admits and the isolated check's init tool set now count thirteen mcp__escher tools; the fake server answers graph with an empty nodes and states object; the capability-unused set is unchanged, graph not required of a cold agent.

The MCP listing now holds thirteen tools with graph after lint; graph joins the closed sets of the tool_call span's tool and the command span's verb, a graph command line recording verb alone, no span field added.

The capability-statement pin now reads thirteen verbs and fourteen node keys in the capability doc and the thirteen driver commands as tools in the readme, all green, with no change to the pin's test code; the doc's not-built reacts-to-a-click line is retired.
The two committed Counter checks (command-line and MCP) were re-recorded through record_checks.sh, the clickable key moving their bytes, and stand_replay replays them green.

The stand shared table module gained the Drive enum and GRAPH_DRIVES, seven rows; the session shared module gained the graph call builder and the graphed reader, so its reader count and the shared table module's reader count can move with stand_graph.
The stand-repeat leg's stand_ glob now takes stand_graph; the seventeen named non-stand targets are unchanged.
The stand non-lean tasks check gained the CLICKABLE table and a clickable-without-role count; the listener mark count stays 677.

The session-over-held-instance boundary gains a read-only verb: graph runs no step, changes nothing, holds no typed text, feeds the record of ids from the graph's node ids, and an argument to it is refused malformed with nothing run.

The host and mcp-role log checks now make one graph call each and read 0 id, component and state-name needles at trace under both builds, through a new graph_needles helper in seven_guis' shared test module.

The bridge test child gained a dispatch test, and DioxusDocument gained a cfg(test) dispatch_to_vdom: any standing statement that no function under test gained a cfg(test) shim is no longer true of the bridge tests.

The bridge dispatch, DioxusEventHandler::handle_event, now sets and clears the registry's dispatch where a SignalRegistry is provided at the root, a change on every Dioxus document's event path, inert without a registry; the buffered render, initial_build, poll and flush_queued_mounted_events are untouched.

The stable element id grammar gains a reserved fifth form owner///key; element_id's tests gain a no-id-holds-the-separator check and a virtual_node_id check, every earlier element_id test reading as before.

The escher-driver unit count stays at 100: the JSON forms, schema, command, describe, MCP, recording and command-line tests extend existing cases with graph and clickable rows; its unit coverage list now includes the graph verb's schema and JSON form.
The driver command-span check gains one graph read per layout mode, a command line recording verb alone.
The command-line and MCP child checks each gain a graph case answering one JSON line of the UI graph.
The per-crate coverage floor of dioxus-native-dom (83 %) now covers the two new modules graph and signal_registry; the floor value is unchanged.
The seven_guis tasks register their signals through a use_graph_signal wrapper with declarations read off the code; the stand shell's active signal and stand.rs's linked stay plain use_signal.

body_fields.fact: stand_graph holds six tests over both layout modes: Counter's count declared at boot and confirmed after a click, every stand task's declarations agreeing with its code once its handlers have run, the served screens' handlers, owners and clicks, every graph node a snapshot node with no served id holding the reserved owner///key form, a graph read changing nothing and holding no typed text, and the whole Cells answer within the answer bound; the graph verb equals DioxusDocument::graph on every read.

graph::tests pins the UI graph reader: each node's component, current listeners with mounted included and a removed one gone, a declared write reading declared before a dispatch and confirmed after, two reader components reading a state the writer does not, an option owned by its select, a prefix declaration naming its elements alone, a drifted declaration reading both flags, a write by an element since gone not handed to its ancestor, and a repeated name reading its ordinal with a page holding no state reading none.

signal_registry::tests pins the registry, its mechanism control first: a handler's write recorded against its dispatch and one outside any dispatch against none, a state's entry leaving with its scope and its Debug printing counts only, a declaration naming its element or its prefix, and a page with no registered state holding no registry.

the bridge test a_dispatch_is_recorded_where_a_state_is_registered_and_acts_as_before_where_none_is drives the dispatch through a cfg(test) DioxusDocument::dispatch_to_vdom and reads the registry's dispatch record.
the snapshot unit test an_element_with_an_app_click_listener_reads_clickable pins NodeState.clickable: true where the element's current listeners hold click and it is no disabled form control.

element_id's tests no_id_the_walk_writes_holds_the_virtual_separator and a_virtual_node_id_spells_the_reserved_form_and_names_no_element pin the reserved owner///key form over an adversarial page; virtual_node_id returns None for an empty or slash-bearing key and no caller produces one.

GRAPH_DRIVES in the stand shared table module (seven rows of Drive steps) drives each stand task's conditional writes once; Cells clicks A0, C0, A0 and leaves its keyed editor once by Enter and once by Tab, so no stand write reads unconfirmed or undeclared.

the CLICKABLE table of stand_non_lean_tasks reads clickable-without-role counts per task in both layout modes: Counter, Flight Booker, Timer, CRUD and Temperature Converter 0 each, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676; counter-increment reads clickable, counter-value and cells-grid do not.

the Cells graph answer measured 293,869 bytes on a fresh start cells (547,685 at first build, 522,692 after the readers narrowing); graph takes no argument and answers the whole screen at once, the stated limit An unpaged graph owned by residual res-7cc5bi4k, target next.
the graph verb is exercised as a process by cli_commands graph_answers_one_line_of_the_ui_graph and over the mcp child by mcp_server a_graph_tool_call_answers_its_line_of_the_ui_graph.

stand_mcp_tools a_graph_tool_call_answers_the_readers_graph_and_parents_a_command_recording_its_verb_alone holds the graph tool call in process in both layout modes, its tool_call span parenting one command span recording verb alone.
a graph answer carries ids, component names, handler event names, state names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value: a sentinel typed into crud-name occurs 0 times in it.

a stated limit of the graph's checks: unconfirmed fires only once a dispatch of the handler's event passed through its element and no run wrote the state; a conditional write a run skipped stays unflagged, a stated limit on the operator's word.
